edits.before: Week 7 uses this narrowly and on purpose. It is evidence that sensory load is measurable, setting-specific and comparable against a control group — so “overload” is not just the course's word for a feeling. And it lands on the week's least comfortable section: the runbook tells you who to contact when things go badly, and this is a study saying that one of those settings is aversive and that people in it feel misunderstood. The finding is about health care in Sweden, not lecture theatres, and the week does not stretch it past that.
edits.after: Week 7 uses this when planning how to seek help: the plan may need to account for sensory and communication barriers in the service itself. The findings concern health care in Sweden, not lecture theatres.
edits.reason: Retain the practical consequence and setting limit without announcing deliberate care or defending the course's vocabulary.
